title: SWR, feed lines and dummy loads
blurb: Explain what SWR and a dummy load are for, how to measure them, and what makes feed lines lose power or fail.

T7C01.why: A dummy load absorbs your power as heat, so **tests don't transmit over the air**.
T7C01.trap: It doesn't improve antennas or receivers. It just stands in for the antenna.

T7C02.why: An **antenna analyzer** sweeps frequencies and shows where the antenna is resonant.
T7C02.trap: A frequency counter reads a signal's frequency; it can't tell you if an antenna is resonant.

T7C03.why: A typical dummy load is a **50 Ω non-inductive resistor** on a heat sink: it matches the line and gets rid of the heat.
T7C03.trap: Inductive reactance or relays make it a poor stand-in for a plain 50 Ω antenna.

T7C04.why: **1:1** means no mismatch and no reflected power.
T7C04.trap: SWR is a ratio with 1:1 as the minimum, so it never reads zero.

T7C05.why: Reflected power from high SWR can damage the output transistors, so the transmitter **reduces power to protect them**.
T7C05.trap: Reducing power doesn't lower the SWR. The mismatch is still there.

T7C06.why: Anything much above 1:1 means an **impedance mismatch**. 4:1 is a poor match.
T7C06.trap: SWR is a ratio, not dB of loss or gain.

T7C07.why: Power lost in a feed line is **converted into heat**.
T7C07.trap: Loss doesn't raise SWR or make harmonics.

T7C08.why: A **directional wattmeter** reads forward and reflected power, and SWR follows from those two.
T7C08.trap: Voltmeters and ohmmeters measure DC quantities, not reflected power.

T7C09.why: **Moisture** getting into the cable is a main cause of coax failure.
T7C09.trap: Fluctuating power or full duty cycle doesn't wear out good coax.

T7C10.why: UV damages the jacket, and a cracked jacket **lets water into the cable**.
T7C10.trap: UV doesn't mix with RF or change the conductors' resistance. The harm is the water.

T7C11.why: Foam is mostly air, so foam-dielectric coax has **less loss per foot** than solid.
T7C11.trap: Moisture resistance, voltage breakdown and the 50 Ω match aren't foam's advantage.
